seventeen-countries-one-at-a-time.html.title: Seventeen jurisdictions, fifteen in Europe and around the Mediterranean, two in East Asia
What the 340 charts were drawn from: 21.4 million records, 16.7 million of them Czech MPs’ votes
Fixed days: 1 April carries 29.2% of Japan’s new versions, 1 January 11.6% of France’s and 9.9% of Spain’s
The rule’s day: 95% of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s laws take effect on the eighth day after publication; Spain’s now rarely wait the Civil Code’s twenty
The week: 72% of Albania’s laws adopted on a Thursday, 95% of Bulgaria’s State Gazette issues on a Tuesday or a Friday
August, the month without laws: 2 of Albania’s 3,098 laws, and at most 3% of any parliament’s; Algeria is the exception
From signature to the gazette: Spain’s royal decrees from a median of 31 days in 1979 to 1, Albania’s government decisions from 36 in 2009 to 2 in 2025
Lawmaking by the government: in 2020, 125 ordinances in France, 39 royal decree-laws in Spain, 38 normative acts in Albania
Amending laws: 60% of the laws in Croatia, 59% in Bulgaria and 58% of Montenegro’s laws in force amend another law; in Serbia, Andorra and Türkiye, 37% or fewer
One act, many laws: Türkiye’s decree-law 703 changed 144 laws and decree-laws, Czechia’s Act 281/2009 changed 133 acts
The most-amended act in each record: Belgium’s Judicial Code, 613 new versions since 1985; Japan’s Local Tax Act, the provisions of 940 amending laws
Constitutions: Japan’s has kept one text since 1947 and Andorra’s since 1993; Belgium’s has been revised 82 times since 1994, France’s 25 times since 1958
Still as first written: all 103 articles of Japan’s Constitution, 64% of Spain’s 1889 Civil Code, 21% of France’s of 1804
How old the law in force is: 46% of Türkiye’s laws in force and 41% of Japan’s date from before 1990; 87% of Montenegro’s acts from 2010 or later
Late budgets: Bosnia and Herzegovina’s budget law came out after its year had begun in 22 of 27 years; Spain had no budget law for 6 years
Money in the law: Czechia’s minimum wage rose from CSK 2,000 to CZK 22,400, Albania’s from 7,018 to 50,000 lek; dinars, marks and pesetas gave way to the euro
The death penalty: Vietnam cut it from 18 crimes to 10 on 1 July 2025; Algeria’s Penal Code from 33 articles to 23 in 2006, and back to 27 in October 2026
EU law in the text: 48% of Bulgaria’s laws of 2023 name an EU directive or regulation, 58% of Croatia’s in its accession year; Andorra’s mention the EU in 31%
Treaty partners: a neighbour comes first for Czechia (Slovakia), Croatia (Bosnia and Herzegovina) and Serbia (Montenegro); the United States for Türkiye and Bulgaria; Germany for Albania
What each record could show: 17 of 17 dated their law and 15 the day it took effect; only one, Czechia’s, held the votes
How far back each record reaches: France’s to 1539, Spain’s to 1835; 10 of the 17 start in 1989 or later
What the work found wrong in the data: 13 errors in 7 repositories, each noted on its page and left as it is
